answer: A refundable stake bond turns identity creation from free into expensive. To join the economy, each agent locks collateral that is slashed if peers prove it submitted duplicate or fraudulent work, so a sybil operator must fund every fake identity separately — a thousand copies cost a thousand bonds. Honest agents treat the bond as a haven: it is returned in full for good behavior, while attackers lose theirs. A nebula of cheap fake accounts cannot form, because no fable of free influence survives when each new identity carries a real, forfeitable price.
